fields.meta_title: Fitness Assessment Form With PAR-Q+ and Retests | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a fitness assessment form that screens with the PAR-Q+, saves baseline scores and puts every retest beside them. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Fitness Assessment Form That Tracks Every Retest
fields.hero_description: Describe your screening questions and the tests you run. Emergent builds the fitness assessment form, a record for each client and a report that reads every retest against the baseline.
fields.features_heading: What a Fitness Assessment Form Records
fields.features_subheading: Each section answers something a trainer needs on test day, or twelve weeks later at the retest.
fields.feature_1:
PAR-Q+ answers that gate the first test

Open with the seven PAR-Q+ questions. A yes on any of them brings up the matching follow-up pages, and the trainer sees that testing is on hold before the client arrives.
fields.feature_2:
Vitals and measurements in fixed units

Record resting heart rate and blood pressure, then body measurements, as numbers with set units. Readings never land as loose text, which keeps every later retest comparable.
fields.feature_3:
A field for each test and its protocol

Store each test with a line on how it was run, such as a 1-minute plank or a 3-minute step test. Trainers repeat the identical protocol later and the scores line up.
fields.feature_4:
Retests that open with the baseline

Start a retest from the client's record and the earlier scores load first. Each new score saves next to the old one, the change is worked out, and a progress report goes out.
fields.feature_5:
Movement videos kept with the client

Accept squat or gait videos recorded on a phone. Every clip is saved in storage you own under that client's record, where the coach writes notes before planning any training.
fields.feature_6:
Your gym's code, exported whole

Export the form and every client record to your GitHub repository. Host the app on your own servers, or have a developer link it to the booking software your gym uses now.

fields.tab_content_1:
Any yes on the PAR-Q+ holds today's step test

Corwin Athletic Club sends the PAR-Q+ to every new member before the first session. Jordan Hale answers yes to question 2, about chest pain. The form opens the follow-up pages for that answer. Trainer Mia Torres gets a Slack message that the step test is on hold until Jordan completes those pages.
fields.tab_content_2:
Week 0 next to week 12 on one report

Twelve weeks after his first test, Marcus Reed repeats the same tests with the same trainer. The form sets each week 12 score beside week 0. His push-ups rose by 8 to 22 and his plank by 35 seconds to 80. The sit-and-reach gained 5 cm and now reads 29. Marcus gets the one-page report by email.
fields.tab_content_3:
Squat video reviewed before week one is written

Lena Brooks coaches online, and her new clients test at home. Tara Quinn films an overhead squat from the front and the side, then logs her waist and weight. The clips land in Lena's review queue. She notes that Tara's heels lift, and only then does week one of the program go out.
fields.tab_content_4:
Each full day points students at the next opening

The rec center at Northfield State runs free assessments for students in 45-minute slots, 12 a day. When Thursday fills, the booking page offers Friday at 8:00 AM instead. Staff enter scores on a tablet during the session. Each student's results go to that student alone.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Fitness Assessment Form
fields.howto_description: Start with the tests your trainers already run, then decide what has to happen before anyone is tested.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Copy the tests you run now
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask for goals and a retest date
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every test your trainers run today on one page, along with the protocol for each, like push-ups to failure. Cut any test nobody repeated at a retest last year. A score that is never measured twice tells the trainer nothing about progress.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Put the PAR-Q+ ahead of every test field, using the current published version with its wording unchanged. Then decide which staff member hears about a yes answer and what the client sees on screen while the follow-up pages are still open.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Every reading gets a field with a fixed unit: beats per minute, centimeters, seconds or repetitions. Add a short note field for what the trainer saw, such as a client who stopped early. Free text typed into a score field cannot be compared later.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask for one or two goals in the client's own words and pick a retest interval, for example every 8 or 12 weeks. The form dates the retest from the first session and reminds the trainer a week ahead, with the earlier scores attached.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste into the prompt your question list, each test with its unit and how often clients come back. Emergent builds the form with a client database and a progress report behind it. Add a test later, such as a 1.5-mile run, by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_6_des: A retest is only fair when the client arrives in the same state as at the first visit. Send a note on booking with your gym's prep rules, such as no hard exercise in the 24 hours before testing.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Before the form goes live, submit a sample member who answers yes on the PAR-Q+, then one with a full set of scores and one back for a retest. Check that each one lands where your staff expect it.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is paper and one-off templates: NASM's resource page of PDFs, NSCA's printable sheet with a pre-test and a post-test column, a University of Tennessee form on pdfFiller, an NCHPAD testing handout, Pinterest pins, an OPEX blog post and two builder templates (Jotform, 123FormBuilder). Each one collects the answers once and stops. A fitness assessment is two events weeks apart, and the form is only useful if the second one is read against the first. This page treats the form as the client's testing record: PAR-Q+ answers decide whether testing goes ahead today, baseline scores are saved per client, and the retest lands next to the baseline with the change worked out. It stays off goals, packages and scheduling (the personal training intake page) and off go/follow-up screening events (the health screening page).

claims_to_source: The PAR-Q+ opens with seven general health questions, and a yes to any of them leads to follow-up questions
ACSM's preparticipation screening looks at current exercise participation, known cardiovascular, metabolic or renal disease or its signs and symptoms, and the intended exercise intensity
The five health-related components of fitness are cardiorespiratory endurance, muscular strength, muscular endurance, flexibility and body composition
NSCA's fitness assessment form records a pre-test date and a post-test date with scores for each
Common assessment tests include a step test, a push-up test and a sit-and-reach test
Clients are told to skip food, caffeine and tobacco for three hours and hard exercise for 24 hours before testing
The 3-3-3 rule is a workout format: three workouts a week, three exercises a session, three sets each
